entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hanno, son of Hannibal, was a Carthaginian general during the First Punic War (264-241 BCE).

He led a military expedition to the western coast of Africa, specifically the region now known as Morocco, in search of gold and new trade routes.

This voyage, known as the First Expedition of Hanno, was documented by the Greek historian Diodorus Siculus and is considered one of the earliest recorded European explorations.

The expedition's significance lies in its demonstration of Carthaginian maritime power and its potential to challenge the dominance of the Phoenician and Greek empires.

The legacy of Hanno's expedition can be seen in the later European explorers who followed in his footsteps, such as the Romans and the Portuguese.

Hanno's discovery of the Atlantic Ocean and his attempts to establish trade relations with the indigenous peoples of Africa paved the way for centuries of European colonization and the scramble for Africa.

The explorer's name has become synonymous with the idea of European exploration and the quest for wealth and knowledge in the ancient world.
